title: The Phantom Warning
text: I was drifting through town, lost in thought, when I stepped into the street without looking. A piercing shriek sliced through the air—an old woman screamed for me to stop. I froze just in time to see a bus thunder past. When I turned to thank her, the street was empty. No trace of her remained. That evening, I saw a photograph of my grandmother, who had died seven years ago. She was wearing the same floral scarf described by the witnesses.

title: The Pianist's Lament
text: We wandered into the skeleton of an abandoned theater, its air thick with forgotten breath. As we crept through its crumbling halls, a piano melody began to drift low and haunting, almost mournful. It drew us to the stage, where a dust-veiled piano sat, keys untouched, strings long dead. Then he appeared: a tall, gaunt figure in tattered evening wear, standing in the balcony like a relic of grief. He stared down at us, his eyes hollow with memory, before dissolving into nothingness. Later, we learned of the fire—the pianist who perished mid-performance, still searching for his final ovation.

title: Footsteps in the Fog
text: The fog rolled across the narrow cobblestone street, swallowing the old buildings one by one. I heard footsteps behind me, slow and deliberate, matching every step I took. Whenever I turned around, the street was empty. Suddenly, a cold hand brushed against my shoulder, and a whisper reached my ear: 'You came back.' I ran until I reached the main road. The following morning, I discovered that the street had been closed for decades after a mysterious disappearance.

title: The Woman at the Lighthouse
text: I was photographing the lighthouse during a storm when I noticed a woman standing at the edge of the cliff. Her white dress moved in the wind, but she remained perfectly still. I called out, warning her to step away from the edge. She slowly turned toward me, revealing a face as pale as the moon. Lightning flashed, and she vanished. When I checked my photographs later, every image showed the lighthouse clearly, except one. In that photograph, a second figure stood directly behind me.

title: The Last Train
text: I boarded the nearly empty train just before midnight. At the far end of the carriage, an elderly man sat staring at the floor, clutching a newspaper dated 1947. He looked up and asked whether the station was still burning. Confused, I told him there was no fire. The train entered a tunnel, and all the lights went out for several seconds. When they returned, the man had disappeared. At the next station, an employee told me that the train had been involved in a fatal accident decades earlier.

title: The Knocking Upstairs
text: I had been living alone in the old house for only three nights when the knocking began. Every night at exactly 1:20 AM, three heavy knocks came from the ceiling above my bedroom. I assumed it was a neighbor until I remembered that my apartment was on the top floor. On the fourth night, I climbed into the attic with a flashlight. There were no footprints, no furniture, and no signs of anyone entering. Then three knocks sounded directly behind me, from inside the locked attic door.
